extraction.name: IFEval (Instruction-Following Eval)
extraction.description: IFEval is an evaluation benchmark designed to assess the instruction-following capabilities of Large Language Models. It focuses on 25 types of verifiable instructions (such as length constraints, detectable formats, and keyword inclusions) across 541 prompts that can be verified objectively and deterministically by code.
extraction.creator: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Prompts were created through a four-step process: (1) generating a set of base prompts with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions appended, (2) using few-shot prompting to identify and remove illogical prompts, (3) applying few-shot prompting to rephrase prompts to increase phrasing diversity, and (4) manually checking and editing the rephrased prompts one by one.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Illogical prompts with conflicting instructions were filtered out using few-shot prompting before rephrasing and manual review.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Verification is automated via deterministic programs that verify compliance with verifiable instructions. Compliance is assessed under both strict criteria (exact adherence) and loose criteria (applying up to eight combinations of transformation functions: stripping markdown font modifiers, removing the first line, and removing the last line).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors analyze trade-offs between false negatives and false positives in automated rule-based evaluation. While naive string matches produce false negatives due to markdown formatting or conversational filler, heuristic response transformations used in loose evaluation reduce false negatives but may introduce false positives.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Deterministic Python verification scripts and rule-based heuristic checking functions
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Accurate instruction-following in LLMs is highlighted as critical for system safety and reliability, preventing unintended or harmful outputs in high-stakes settings such as healthcare or autonomous systems.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Very few instructions are completely verifiable objectively and automatically due to edge cases. Loose evaluation criteria may introduce false positives. The benchmark is currently limited to 25 verifiable instruction categories and text-only tasks, lacking multi-modal instruction verification.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating the instruction-following capabilities of Large Language Models.
